_comment: 🧩️ DOCX ECMA-376/✳️any's own contribution to the repository test platform -- its mutation oracle registration and its declared mutation vocabulary (wave 7, ticket 26/08/23/END-TO-END-TESTING-REFACTOR). A DOCX is a ZIP of XML parts, and both `zip` 6 and `quick-xml` 0.42 are already linked and are genuinely independent of this repository's own codec: `zip` unzips/rezips the OPC container, `quick-xml` parses/edits/re-serializes the OOXML parts (word/document.xml, word/styles.xml, [Content_Types].xml, every *.rels). Registered as ONE oracle entry naming the composition -- neither library alone reads a DOCX; the pair together is the real independent implementation, and this subset's own oracle module (../🦀️oracle.rs) is the composition code, not a third dependency.

oracles.rationale:
🫥️ RECLASSIFIED by the `reimplementation-registered-as-third-party` gate. The crate named here does real work — it parses and writes this format — but what a MUTATION SHOULD PRODUCE is computed by this owner's own `🦀️oracle.rs`. Both halves of the comparison then descend from ONE reading of the specification, so a misreading of it yields two agreeing wrong answers: the single failure a differential test exists to prevent.

The honest split is that the crate discharges "the result is a well-formed file of this format" and NOT "the mutation computed the right answer". Only the second is what a mutation oracle is for, so this is a `cross-semio-implementation` — a required SUPPLEMENT, never a substitute, and a qualifying third-party reference is still owed.

Any fixtures registered alongside are untouched and remain valuable: real bytes of the real format, byte-reproducible, and exactly what a qualifying reader gets pointed at the day one is registered.

📖️ A READER, and that is the whole point of registering it separately.

This subset also carries a `🦀️oracle.rs` that COMPUTES what each mutation should produce. That entry is registered `cross-semio-implementation` and does not discharge anything, because both halves of such a comparison descend from one reading of the specification.

This entry is a different mechanism. The expected state is not computed at all — it is COMMITTED, as the `after` half of a byte-reproducible fixture. `jszip` 3.10.1 then parses the ECMA-376 OPC package on BOTH sides and the comparison is over what it recovered. The probes say so in their own header: "Everything here MARSHALS and READS; nothing here applies a mutation or predicts what one should."

So the judge is a third-party implementation of the format, and nothing in this repository predicts the answer it is judging. That is what makes it qualifying where the sibling entry is not.

comparisonProfiles.description: DOCX documents compared by the typed semantic view this subset's own `DocxDocument` models: `body` (the ordered w:body block tree -- paragraphs with their style reference and ordered runs, tables with their ordered rows/cells, recursively) and `styles` (the ordered w:styles list, id/name/basedOn), both order-sensitive per WordprocessingML's own document-order semantics. Every OTHER real OPC part (docProps/*, any part touched only through SetPart/RemovePart) is compared by content-type plus content digest, projected as an unordered path-keyed map so writer-freedom part ORDER never registers as a difference. word/document.xml and word/styles.xml themselves are excluded from that raw-part map: two independent writers legitimately differ byte-for-byte on non-semantic whitespace/attribute-order/self-closing-form for the exact same document, which is exactly why the typed body/styles projection exists instead. [Content_Types].xml and every *.rels part are pure OPC plumbing, regenerated deterministically from the typed content-types/relationships tables on every re-encode by both sides, and are not part of the comparison at all -- neither side's typed mutation vocabulary (13 kinds: NoMutation, SetSnapshot, InsertBlock, RemoveBlock, SetBlockContent, SetRunText, SetRunFormatting, InsertStyle, RemoveStyle, SetStyleName, SetStyleBasedOn, SetPart, RemovePart) ever targets them directly.
Bundle-style comparison for the jszip+fast-xml-parser oracle: delegates to the docx-ecma-376-jszip-compare-v1 pipeline rather than a single-projection diff.

comparisonPipelines.description: Reads the subject's produced docx and the fixture's own expected docx with an independent jszip+fast-xml-parser composition, then compares their typed body/styles projections plus the unordered other-parts digest map. GATING.

stages.description: An independent reader accepts both files.
Order-sensitive body/styles structural equality plus unordered other-parts digest equality — the operative equality.

probes.rationale: An INDEPENDENT reader accepts both files at all. Nothing downstream means anything if one of them does not parse.

qualification.evidence: Run against every generated fixture pair this session (25 recipes, 43 files) — bothImport true in every case.

criteria.detail: parses [Content_Types].xml + word/document.xml + word/styles.xml + every other OPC part
jszip and fast-xml-parser are both pure-JS, already vendored in node_modules

probes.rationale: The typed projection every comparison is measured against — the ordered body block tree (paragraphs with style ref + ordered runs, tables with ordered rows/cells recursively), the ordered styles list (id/name/basedOn), and every other real OPC part as a path-keyed content-type+digest map.

qualification.evidence: Run against insert-block-appends-a-pricing-table/after.docx: reports blockCount 3 with the appended 2×2 table's rows/cells/paragraphs recovered correctly, and against set-part-adds-core-properties/after.docx: reports otherPartCount 1 for docProps/core.xml with the correct resolved content type.

criteria.detail: paragraph and table blocks recovered in document order, xml:space=preserve text kept intact
id/name/basedOn recovered in word/styles.xml document order

probes.rationale: Order-sensitive structural deep-equal over body/styles plus unordered digest equality over every other OPC part — the GATING comparison. Computes no mutation semantics, only structural equality of two already-existing byte blobs.

qualification.evidence: Validated BOTH ways this session with real measured numbers: no-mutation-no-op's identical before/after pair -> {equal:true, diffCount:0}; that same before against a deliberately corrupted copy (word/styles.xml's Heading1 name replaced with "CORRUPTED HEADING") -> {equal:false, diffCount:1, diffs:["$.styles[0].name: \"heading 1\" \u2260 \"CORRUPTED HEADING\""]}. Also exercised on a genuine applied mutation: bolds-the-tower-run-of-the-opening-paragraph's before/after -> {equal:false, diffCount:1, diffs:["$.body[0].runs[1].bold: false \u2260 true"]}.
